verdict.rationale: Fly.io explicitly documents this promise: the same primitives at every scale, no rearchitecting and no platform migration, with 'the API you start with is the API you keep.' It backs this with Fly Machines, which are driven by one REST API and documented to scale out to tens of thousands of VMs, plus `fly scale` for horizontal and vertical growth. Community reports of teams leaving for AWS or Kubernetes cite reliability and support problems, not API discontinuity, so they lower confidence but do not contradict the claim. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of running the same primitives unchanged at large scale, and detailed docs on scale limits or growth paths beyond marketing statements.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the same core APIs and primitives from prototype through massive scale, without rearchitecting or migrating platforms as usage grows

citations.quote: Keep the same primitives at every scale: no rearchitecting when you grow, and no platform migration when you get big. The API you start with is the API you keep.
Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users, and scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives.
Fly Machines are fast-launching VMs with a simple REST API.
the `fly scale` command for quick horizontal and vertical scaling
